text:
The evidence is **consistent with a pine plantation harvest, but does not establish the cause**.

In 2021, 81.3 hectares of tree-cover loss were detected. Of that area, 68.1 hectares overlapped forest mapped as planted pine; 13.2 hectares lay outside mapped forest. The JRC reference mapped 98% of the loss area as forest in 2020.

These observations support that most of the loss occurred in a pine plantation, but they do not distinguish timber harvest from other causes such as fire, storm damage or disease.
